subject: gk
question: Youth Spiritual Summit held in July 2025 was organized by which of the following?

options.text: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Youth Spiritual Summit** held in **July 2025** was organized by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**. This ministry is primarily responsible for developing and empowering youth in India.
 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** aims to engage young minds in holistic development by promoting initiatives like leadership skills, cultural awareness, and spiritual growth.
 
• The focus of the **Youth Spiritual Summit 2025** was to foster spiritual education and moral values among the youth, aligning with broader objectives of national development.
 
• Through such initiatives, the ministry seeks to encourage the youth to contribute positively to society while also promoting mental well-being and emotional stability.
 
• The summit also highlighted the importance of **spirituality as a tool for self-growth** and personal empowerment, resonating with the government’s agenda of nurturing well-rounded, responsible individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports:**

 
 
• Established in **1985**, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports is responsible for promoting youth development and sports activities across India.
 
• Programs under this ministry include the **National Youth Policy**, **National Service Scheme (NSS)**, and **National Youth Festivals**, among others.
 
• The ministry works to cultivate leadership and instill a sense of national integration and responsibility among the youth.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Youth in Nation-Building:**
 
 
• Youth represent around **34% of the Indian population**, making them a significant demographic for driving change and progress.
 
• Engaging youth in programs like spiritual summits helps create a balance between technological advancement and ethical, moral grounding.
 
 
 
• **Spirituality and Youth:**
 
 
• Studies suggest that **spiritual practices** can improve mental health, reduce stress, and foster resilience among young individuals.
 
• Events like the **Youth Spiritual Summit** bring attention to the importance of self-awareness and mindfulness.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Ministries:**
 
• **NITI Aayog:** 
 
 
• Established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.
 
• Full Form: National Institution for Transforming India.
 
• Chairperson: The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio Chairperson.
 
• Objective: To promote Cooperative Federalism and involve states in policy-making.
 
• Nature: It works as the policy think tank of the Government of India.
 
• Major Initiatives: Aspirational Districts Programme and monitoring of SDGs.
 
• Headquarters: New Delhi.
 
• First CEO: Amitabh Kant (2016–2022).
 
• Present CEO: B. V. R. Subrahmanyam (2023–Present).
 
 
 
• **TATA Trusts:** A philanthropic organization that supports various social causes but does not have direct government involvement in youth-related summits.
 
• **Ministry of Education:** Primarily focuses on academic and skill-based programs rather than spiritual initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Youth Policy 2014:**

 
 
• This policy aims to empower youth (15-29 years) to achieve their full potential and contribute to India’s development.
 
• It emphasizes the need for **education, employment, entrepreneurship, and well-being**.
 
 
 
• **National Service Scheme (NSS):**
 
 
• Introduced in **1969**, NSS engages students in community service, fostering a sense of social responsibility and leadership.
 
 
 
• **Fit India Movement:**
 
 
• Launched in **2019** by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to promote fitness and a healthy lifestyle among Indians.
